To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NO-donating compounds 14b-15a were designed, synthesized and evaluated as apoptosis inducers.
a series of NO donating derivatives of scutellarin have been synthesized and the most potent compound 14b has shown significant anti-tumor activity in HepG2 and HCT116 cell lines.
scutellarin and its derivatives are potential anticancer agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel scutellarin-based NO-donating derivatives with high antiproliferation activities, low cytotoxicity and good selectivity between malignant liver cells and normal liver cells.

the development of novel scutellarin-based compounds with potential antitumor activity and low toxicity, which could be used as a lead compound for further optimization and development of novel antitumor drugs.
the design, synthesis and biological activities of a new class of NO-donors based on the scutellarin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NO-releasing scutellarin analogues are promising apoptosis inducers for cancer therapy.
the NO-releasing scutellarin derivative 14b has a great potential as a new drug against liver cancer.
NO-donating derivatives of scutellarin are promising antitumor agents and 14b could be a potential drug candidate for liver cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NO-releasing derivatives of scutellarin have been successfully synthesized and evaluated for their antiproliferation activities and mechanisms of action.
the NO donor scutellarin could be a promising lead structure for the development of antitumor drugs.
the NO-donating derivatives of scutellarin could induce apoptosis in HepG2 and S-phase arrest in PC-3 cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
scutellarin can be a good starting scaffold to design and discover novel antitumor drugs with low toxicity.
scutellarin and its derivatives are a promising source of new antitumor agents.
the NO-donating derivatives of scutellarin are promising antitumor agents, which can be used as lead compounds for the development of novel drugs for liver cancer treatment.
